headline: How much capacity do longer routings and disruptions absorb?

pages.title: Longer routes absorb vessel capacity
points: Red Sea security threats forced carriers round the Cape of Good Hope
Asia–Europe voyages about 10 days longer in one direction
UNCTAD: container ship demand up about 12% from rerouting
Suez ~10,000 nm, 31 days · Cape ~13,000 nm, 41 days
More vessels needed to keep the same weekly frequency

screens.title: Operational disruptions: how much capacity is lost?

cards.head: 1. Port congestion
points: More than 10% of global container capacity reportedly tied up in November 2026
Ships waiting outside ports for available berths cannot begin their next voyage
Terminal bottlenecks and vessel bunching increase waiting times
Weather disruptions can further delay port operations

cards.head: 2. Vessel delays
points: Approximately 5% of global deep-sea container capacity absorbed by vessel delays in August 2026
Late arrivals and missed schedules reduce productive vessel time
Delays at one port can affect the entire shipping rotation
Ships complete fewer voyages over a given period

cards.head: 3. Cape route diversions
points: Estimated share of global capacity absorbed by longer routing in September 2026
Longer rotations mean fewer trips per ship each year
More vessels are needed to maintain existing shipping schedules

screens.title: Impact on the global shipping market

head: Without disruptions
With disruptions
rows: Vessels spend longer sailing and waiting
Potential downward pressure on freight rates

flow.head: 1. Fleet keeps growing
points: New container vessels continue entering the market
Fleet capacity can grow faster than cargo demand

flow.head: 2. Ships spend longer sailing or waiting
points: Longer routes increase voyage durations
Port congestion creates additional waiting times
Vessels become unavailable for their next rotation for longer

flow.head: 3. Effective capacity falls
points: Fewer vessel-days are available for transporting cargo
The same fleet completes fewer trips over a given period
Additional capacity is absorbed by operational inefficiencies

flow.head: 4. Overcapacity is temporarily delayed
points: Some of the additional supply pressure is temporarily masked
The market may appear tighter than the underlying fleet-demand balance suggests
Shipping capacity can become available again when disruptions ease

capacity.nominal: Nominal capacity: total capacity of the global container fleet
capacity.effective: Effective capacity: capacity actually available after time lost to longer sailing routes, port waiting and operational disruptions
